newsitem.title: USA: Federal court denies Missouri smokers class status.
newsitem.headline: Federal court denies Missouri smokers class status.

text.p: A federal district court has denied a motion to certify a class of all Missouri residents claiming injury as a result of smoking cigarettes manufactured by Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, the company said Tuesday.

The denial of class certification results in dismissal of the class-wide allegations in the Missouri litigation, known as Smith, the company explained. Brown & Williamson is owned by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc.

In late December, the court -- the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Missouri, Western Division -- dismissed B.A.T from the suit for lack of personal jurisdiction. The case was originally filed by the plantiff, Barbara Smith, in state court in March 1996, then removed to federal court, B&W spokesman Tom Fitzgerald said.

Although Judge Ortrie D. Smith found that potential members in the class action claimed certain common issues in a general sense, "resolution of these issues will have little to no legal or practical significance for this case," B&W quoted the judge as saying.
In light of the significant individual issues in the case, Judge Smith found certification of a class would not promote judicial economy, but would rather "create judicial diseconomy," B&W said.
"We are very pleased with the court's decision," Gary Long, attorney for B&W, said of the May 22 decision.
The company learned about the decision over the Memorial Day weekend, Fitzgerald said.

As the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals pointed out in its Castano decision, Long continued, "class actions are not an appropriate way to handle these cases. Each plaintiff's case is unique and will turn on dominant individual issues, and such cases are simply not suitable for resolution on a class-wide basis."

The company said Judge Smith also rejected the plaintiff's request to decide entitlement to punitive damages on a common basis on the grounds that such a procedure would radically alter appropriate consideration of this issue and might violate Missouri law.
Headquartered in Louisville, Ky., Brown & Williamson is the manufacturer and marketer of cigarette brands such as Kool, Lucky Strike, GPC, Misty and Carlton.
